title: Crystal Trade Profit
statement:
The outpost logs the price of an alien energy crystal on each of `n` days, `prices[i]`. Choose a single day to buy and a later day to sell to maximize profit. Return 0 if no profit is possible.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(prices) <= 10^5
- 0 <= prices[i] <= 10^4
hint: Track the lowest price seen so far as you scan once; at each day, check the profit if you sold today at that low.

title: Echo Detector
statement:
A log of transmission signal IDs `nums` may contain the same ID twice within a suspiciously short window. Given an integer `k`, return True if two equal values exist at indices `i` and `j` with `abs(i - j) <= k`.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- 0 <= k <= len(nums)
hint: Keep a hash map of each value's most recent index as you scan. If you see a value again within k of its last index, you're done.

title: Peak Energy Window
statement:
The outpost's sensor logs `nums` energy readings, one per cycle. Find the maximum total energy across any `k` consecutive cycles.

Constraints:
- 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
hint: Compute the sum of the first window of size k, then slide it: add the entering value and subtract the one leaving, tracking the best total seen.

title: Steady Pulse Streak
statement:
A binary sensor log `nums` marks each cycle as stable (1) or unstable (0). Return the length of the longest streak of consecutive stable cycles.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- nums[i] is 0 or 1
hint: Track a running streak counter: reset it to 0 on a 0, increment it on a 1, and keep the best value seen.

title: The Unique Glyph Run
statement:
A string `s` of alien glyphs was intercepted. Find the length of the longest contiguous run containing no repeated glyph.

Constraints:
- 0 <= len(s) <= 5 * 10^4
- s consists of printable ASCII characters
hint: Grow the window's right edge, tracking the last-seen index of each glyph. When you hit a repeat inside the window, jump the left edge past its previous occurrence.

title: The Shortest Surge
statement:
A stream of positive energy readings `nums` must reach a `target` total. Find the length of the shortest contiguous run of readings whose sum is at least `target`. Return 0 if no such run exists.

Constraints:
- 1 <= target <= 10^9
- 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5
- 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4
hint: Grow the window's right edge, adding to a running sum. Whenever the sum reaches target, shrink from the left as much as possible while tracking the shortest length found.

title: Frequency Stabilizer
statement:
A string `s` of alien glyphs can have up to `k` glyphs swapped for any other glyph. Find the length of the longest substring achievable where every glyph in it is the same, after at most `k` swaps.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(s) <= 5 * 10^4
- s consists of uppercase English letters
- 0 <= k <= len(s)
hint: Track the count of each glyph inside the window and the highest single-glyph count seen. The window is valid as long as (window size - highest count) <= k; shrink from the left when it isn't.

title: The Hidden Broadcast
statement:
Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, return True if `s2` contains a contiguous substring that is some rearrangement (permutation) of `s1`.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(s1), len(s2) <= 10^4
- s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters
hint: Use a fixed-size window of length len(s1) sliding across s2, comparing letter-frequency counts of the window against s1's frequency count.

title: Two-Species Sampling
statement:
A row of alien fruit species was recorded as they were encountered, `fruits[i]`. A sampling basket can carry at most two distinct species at once. Find the length of the longest contiguous run of fruit that a single basket can collect.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(fruits) <= 10^5
hint: This is 'longest substring with at most 2 distinct values.' Track counts of each species in the window; shrink from the left whenever a third distinct species appears.

title: The Full-Spectrum Window
statement:
BOSS TRIAL — Intercepted transmission `s` must be scanned for the shortest contiguous window that contains every glyph required by `t` (including repeats — if `t` needs a glyph twice, the window must contain it at least twice too). Return that minimal window, or an empty string if no such window exists.

Constraints:
- 1 <= len(s), len(t) <= 5 * 10^4
- s and t consist of English letters
hint: Track how many of each required glyph the window still needs. Grow the right edge until every requirement is met, then greedily shrink the left edge while it stays valid, recording the shortest valid window.
